text.en:
Tara lives in a hill village and Arun lives in a town on a wide plain.
When Tara visits, Arun says, "Your road is so steep!"
"And your fields are so flat!" says Tara. "Our houses and our work are different because our land is different."

The land around us shapes how people live. In mountains the land is steep and the weather is cold, so farming is difficult. People grow crops on terraces cut into slopes, keep sheep and goats, and work in tourism and forests.
Plains are flat and have fertile soil and rivers. It is easy to grow crops, build roads, railways and cities. Most people in India live on plains such as the Ganga plain.
People adapt their houses, clothes and food to the land: sloping roofs and woollen clothes in cold hills, and light cotton clothes in hot plains.
In mountains the land is steep and cold, so farming is hard. People make steps on the slopes called terraces.
Plains are flat with fertile soil and rivers. Farming, roads and cities are easy to build.
Most people live on plains. The Ganga plain is one of the most crowded places.
People change their clothes, houses and food to suit the land and the weather.

problem.en: Why do many people live on the plains instead of high mountains?

text.en: Plains are flat and have fertile soil and water.
It is easy to build roads, houses and cities.
So more people can live and work there.

prompt.en: A friend asks why hill people make steps on the slopes. What will you say?

requiredIdeas.en: The slopes are steep, so flat steps called terraces hold soil and water.
Crops can then be grown on them.

points.en: Mountains are steep and cold; people use terraces.
Plains are fertile, so most people live there.
